title: AC-MT207-FixSuggestionApply

scope.summary:
GOAL: Turn a Gerrit-style fix_suggestion attached to an annotation into a one-click, safe, attributable edit: compute the apply PREVIEW diff, apply the replacements through the editor edit pipeline as a SINGLE undo unit, REFUSE with a typed reason when the anchor is OUTDATED/ORPHANED (never apply a fix to code the suggestion no longer describes), and record who applied whose suggestion. This is the payoff of the fix_suggestions field defined in MT-201 and the re-anchor safety of MT-204.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new file src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/fix_apply.rs with the apply-planning + guard logic (I/O-free planning: given the annotation, its fix_suggestions, and current file text, produce an ApplyPlan or a typed refusal); (b) annotations/mod.rs re-export; (c) unit tests. The ACTUAL editor mutation + single-undo-unit commit is performed by the caller (MT-205 route / NA GUI) through the incumbent editor edit pipeline; this MT owns the safe PLAN + guard + the application record shape. NO storage schema changes (reuse the MT-203 receipt path), NO re-anchor math (call MT-204), NO new record fields.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. `fn plan_fix_apply(annotation: &Annotation, suggestion_index: usize, current_text: &str, config) -> Result<ApplyPlan, FixApplyRefusal>`:
   a. FIRST re-anchor the annotation against current_text via the MT-204 engine. If the outcome is OUTDATED or ORPHANED, REFUSE with a typed FixApplyRefusal { reason: AnchorOutdated | AnchorOrphaned, detail } — do NOT apply. Only a REANCHORED (or exact Match) anchor may proceed.
   b. Validate each FixReplacement's ReplacementRange against current_text: on a char boundary, within bounds, non-overlapping across the suggestion's replacements; a violation REFUSES with FixApplyRefusal { reason: ReplacementOutOfBounds | OverlappingReplacements }.
   c. Produce an ApplyPlan { edits: Vec<ResolvedEdit { byte_range, replacement }>, preview_diff (via `similar`), resulting_text_hash } — a deterministic, ordered, non-overlapping edit set the editor pipeline can apply atomically.
2. SINGLE UNDO UNIT: the ApplyPlan is shaped so the caller applies ALL replacements of one suggestion as ONE editor transaction (one undo step), never partial; document the contract that the caller must commit the plan atomically or not at all. Provide the edits pre-sorted end-to-start (or with absolute byte ranges) so applying them cannot invalidate later ranges.
3. APPLICATION RECORD: `ApplicationRecord { annotation_id, suggestion_index, applied_by: AnnotationAuthor (the APPLIER, from identity/session), suggestion_author: AnnotationAuthor (the annotation's author, WHOSE suggestion), applied_at_utc, resulting_text_hash }` — who applied whose suggestion, persisted via the MT-203 receipt path (an ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED EventLedger receipt) by the caller. The applier and the suggestion author are distinct and both recorded.
4. PREVIEW parity: the preview_diff produced here is the same shape MT-205's apply-fix/preview route returns, so preview and apply cannot disagree (compute once, apply the exact plan that was previewed; the resulting_text_hash lets the caller assert the file was unchanged between preview and apply).
5. DETERMINISM + I/O-FREE: plan_fix_apply is a pure function of (annotation, index, current_text, config); no file reads, no storage, no ledger writes here — the caller owns the editor mutation and the receipt. Identical inputs yield an identical plan and hash.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read record.rs (FixSuggestion/FixReplacement/ReplacementRange 0-based half-open UTF-8 columns) and reanchor.rs (ReanchorOutcome) before writing.
2. Implement fix_apply.rs: re-anchor guard first, then range validation, then the ordered non-overlapping ResolvedEdit plan + `similar` preview + resulting hash.
3. Define ApplicationRecord (applier vs suggestion author distinct) and document the caller's single-undo-unit + receipt contract.
4. Unit tests per expected_tests incl. OUTDATED/ORPHANED refusal, overlapping/out-of-bounds refusal, multi-byte UTF-8, and determinism.
5. Run proof targets; keep the module I/O-free and import-clean (seam law).
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml ([[test]] registration for annotation_fix_apply_tests only, if a separate harness is used)
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (the editor edit pipeline + GUI apply affordance are owned by NA family MT-221+; this MT produces the plan they consume)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/record.rs / anchor.rs / reanchor.rs (owned by MT-201/202/204; call, do not edit)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/** (the ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED receipt uses the MT-203 path via the caller)
acceptance_criteria: plan_fix_apply re-anchors via the MT-204 engine FIRST and REFUSES with a typed FixApplyRefusal (AnchorOutdated | AnchorOrphaned) when the anchor is not REANCHORED/Match — a fix is never applied to code the suggestion no longer describes.

Each FixReplacement range is validated (char boundary, in-bounds, non-overlapping) and a violation refuses with a typed ReplacementOutOfBounds | OverlappingReplacements — no partial or corrupting apply.

The ApplyPlan is an ordered, non-overlapping ResolvedEdit set shaped for a SINGLE atomic editor transaction (one undo unit); the edits cannot invalidate one another (absolute byte ranges or end-to-start ordering).
The preview_diff is produced via `similar` and equals the MT-205 preview shape; a resulting_text_hash lets the caller assert the file was unchanged between preview and apply.

ApplicationRecord records the APPLIER and the SUGGESTION AUTHOR as distinct AnnotationAuthors plus applied_at_utc and resulting_text_hash; the caller persists it as an ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED receipt via the MT-203 path.
plan_fix_apply is a pure I/O-free deterministic function of (annotation, index, current_text, config); identical inputs yield an identical plan and hash; multi-byte UTF-8 replacements are correct.
cargo build + clippy clean; fix_apply.rs imports nothing from storage/api/mcp and reuses the MT-204 engine (no re-anchor math inline).
proof_targets: cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml annotation_fix_apply -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
grep -rn 'use crate::\(storage\|api\|mcp\)' src/backend/handshake_core/src/annotations/fix_apply.rs | wc -l | grep -q '^0$' (I/O-free + seam law)
implementation_notes: The re-anchor-first guard is the safety core: a suggestion authored against an older file must NOT be applied to shifted/changed code. Reusing the MT-204 engine (not a fresh check) guarantees the apply gate and the display gate agree on staleness.

fix_suggestions carry 0-based half-open UTF-8 byte-column ranges (MT-201 rustdoc); resolving them to absolute byte edits and applying end-to-start is what keeps a multi-replacement suggestion a single atomic undo unit that cannot self-invalidate.

Applier vs suggestion-author distinction is the accountability requirement: a human operator applying a model's suggestion, or one agent applying another's, must both be recorded — this is who-applied-whose-suggestion, not just who-authored.

This module is I/O-free and produces a PLAN; the caller (MT-205 route / NA GUI) performs the editor mutation through the incumbent edit pipeline as one transaction and writes the ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED receipt via the MT-203 path. Keeping planning pure lets MT-208 prove seam adoption and lets tests run without a DB or editor.
resulting_text_hash guards the preview->apply gap: if the file changed between preview and apply the hash mismatches and the caller must re-preview, preventing a stale plan from corrupting the file.
`similar` (added in MT-204) produces the preview diff; do not add a second diff crate.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/core apply-planning MT; the one-click apply button and undo integration live in the editor/GUI owned by the NA family (MT-221+). This MT delivers the safe plan + guard they consume; observability is the ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED receipt the caller writes.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal apply-planning MT with no direct operator surface; the operator-facing apply action and its manual entry land with the NA GUI (MT-221+) that drives this plan through the editor pipeline.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason at THIS layer — plan_fix_apply is a pure function; the caller emits the ANNOTATION_FIX_APPLIED EventLedger receipt (via the MT-203 path) when it commits the plan.

internal_diagnostics: WIRED — every refusal is a typed FixApplyRefusal variant (AnchorOutdated/AnchorOrphaned/ReplacementOutOfBounds/OverlappingReplacements); no silent partial apply, no stringly error.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — pure, bounded planning; no long-running runtime posture owned here.
risk_if_missed: Without a guarded apply, a one-click fix runs against stale/shifted code (the suggestion no longer describes what it edits), corrupting the file; multi-replacement fixes apply partially or self-invalidate their own ranges; there is no single-undo-unit so a bad apply can't be cleanly reverted; and there is no record of who applied whose suggestion, breaking accountability in a multi-agent steering loop.

risks: RISK-1: Applying a fix to stale code — the apply path skips the re-anchor guard (or uses a different staleness check than the display), so a suggestion authored against an older file mutates shifted/changed code and corrupts it.

RISK-2: Non-atomic / self-invalidating multi-replacement — replacements are applied start-to-end so an early edit shifts later byte ranges, or applied as separate undo steps so a partial apply can't be cleanly reverted.
RISK-3: Out-of-bounds / overlapping / non-boundary replacement ranges are applied without validation, panicking on a byte slice or producing garbled UTF-8.

RISK-4: Preview/apply divergence — the applied edit differs from what was previewed (file changed in between, or the plan is recomputed differently), so the operator commits something they did not see.
RISK-5: Missing accountability — the application records only the suggestion author or only the applier, not both, so who-applied-whose-suggestion is lost in the steering audit.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): plan_fix_apply re-anchors via the MT-204 engine FIRST and refuses on OUTDATED/ORPHANED; refuses_outdated_and_orphaned proves no plan is produced for a stale anchor.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): The ApplyPlan is a single-transaction, absolute-byte-range (or end-to-start ordered) non-overlapping edit set; single_undo_unit_non_overlapping_plan asserts applying the plan cannot invalidate its own ranges and is one undo unit.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Each ReplacementRange is validated (char boundary, in-bounds, non-overlapping) with a typed refusal; a test feeds overlapping and out-of-bounds ranges and asserts refusal, never a panic or garbled apply.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): The plan carries a resulting_text_hash and the preview equals the applied edit set; the caller asserts the current file hash matches the plan's precondition before committing, re-previewing on mismatch.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): ApplicationRecord records applier AND suggestion author as distinct AnnotationAuthors; application_record_applier_vs_suggestion_author_distinct asserts both are present and may differ.

research_provenance.source: Operator-verified annotation research 2026-07-21: Gerrit fix_suggestions / FixReplacement model (description + replacements:[{path, range, replacement}]) is the suggestion shape (defined in MT-201); the re-anchor-first apply guard derives from the Hypothesis/anchor-staleness discipline (a suggestion is only valid against the content it was anchored to) and the umputun/revdiff explicit-orphan policy (an orphaned anchor cannot be applied). Grounding audit of wtc-native-editors-v1: record.rs FixSuggestion/FixReplacement/ReplacementRange (0-based half-open UTF-8 byte columns), reanchor.rs ReanchorOutcome (MT-204), and `similar` (added MT-204) for the preview diff; the editor single-undo-unit contract is the incumbent code-editor edit-pipeline expectation the NA GUI consumes.
corrections: This MT owns the SAFE PLAN + GUARD + application-record shape, not the editor mutation itself: the caller applies the plan through the incumbent editor pipeline as one atomic undo unit and writes the receipt — keeping planning pure and testable without a DB or GUI.
The apply gate reuses the MT-204 engine so the staleness decision that hides/flags an annotation and the one that refuses an apply are the SAME decision — they can never disagree.
Accountability is who-applied-whose-suggestion: applier and suggestion author are distinct recorded identities, not a single 'author' field.
